sources.title: List of cloud types
sources.observation: The article says that among multi-level cloud genera, those with the greatest convective activity are categorized as “towering vertical.” It describes cumulonimbiform towers as the most unstable and convectively active physical form, with very large examples sometimes having tops that penetrate the lower stratosphere. By contrast, it notes that small cumulus are grouped with low clouds because they lack significant vertical extent.

sources.title: Clouds in Tropical Cyclones
sources.observation: The author argues that convective clouds in tropical cyclones can become very deep because intense updrafts develop, especially when high–moist-static-energy air enters the base of the eyewall and intermittently upsets the near-balanced vortex; small-scale subvortices can contain strong, erect updrafts. The paper also describes principal rainbands with convective cells featuring overturning updrafts and notes that distant rainbands consist of cumulonimbus clouds similar to non–tropical storm convection.
